points.description: States that a linked list is a collection of elements (nodes/data items) that can be allocated dynamically (at run time, not fixed size).
points.partial_credit: 2 marks if only half is stated, e.g. says it is a collection/sequence of elements or nodes linked together but does not mention dynamic allocation, or says dynamic but not a collection of elements.

points.description: Uses the idea of dynamic allocation explicitly (memory allocated at run time / grows or shrinks as needed) as the property of the collection.
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if dynamic or flexible size is implied vaguely.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a linked list is a collection of elements (nodes) that are dynamically allocated, in any wording; extra correct detail such as pointers linking nodes is fine. Part marks for naming only one half (a collection of linked nodes with no mention of dynamic allocation, or dynamic memory with no collection). No marks for describing something else, such as an array with fixed size.
